primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Unequal crossover creates a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene in which ACTH-responsive CYP11B1 regulatory sequences drive CYP11B2 aldosterone-synthase coding sequences. Aldosterone synthase is therefore ectopically expressed in the zona fasciculata and aldosterone production becomes ACTH-dependent rather than primarily renin-angiotensin regulated.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy has severe hypertension discovered during a sports physical. Plasma renin activity is suppressed and plasma aldosterone is elevated. His father developed hypertension in adolescence, and a paternal uncle died of a hemorrhagic stroke at age 32. Genetic testing identifies a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene. Low-dose dexamethasone markedly suppresses aldosterone production.
lead: Which of the following molecular changes best explains this patient's disorder?
correct: ACTH-responsive CYP11B1 regulatory sequences drive ectopic expression of aldosterone synthase
distractors: A gain-of-function mutation constitutively activates the mineralocorticoid receptor
Loss of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 permits cortisol to activate the mineralocorticoid receptor
A loss-of-function mutation in the epithelial sodium channel causes renal sodium wasting
An activating mutation in the angiotensin II type 1 receptor makes aldosterone secretion renin independent
distractor_notes: Constitutive mineralocorticoid-receptor activation would produce mineralocorticoid effects but does not explain a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimera or dexamethasone-suppressible aldosterone.
11β-HSD2 loss causes apparent mineralocorticoid excess with low renin and low aldosterone, not ACTH-dependent aldosterone excess.
Loss of ENaC causes salt wasting and hyperkalemia; Liddle syndrome is caused by ENaC gain of function and also has low aldosterone.
The established mechanism of familial hyperaldosteronism type I is the CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene, not an angiotensin-receptor activating mutation.
key_expl: Familial hyperaldosteronism type I is caused by unequal crossover between CYP11B1 and CYP11B2. The resulting chimeric gene places aldosterone-synthase coding sequences under ACTH-responsive CYP11B1 regulation, causing ectopic zona-fasciculata expression and ACTH-dependent aldosterone production. Suppressing ACTH with glucocorticoid therefore suppresses aldosterone.
objective: Explain glucocorticoid-remediable aldosteronism as ACTH-driven aldosterone-synthase expression from a CYP11B1/CYP11B2 chimeric gene.
